info.title: Stackmap API
info.summary: Document your infrastructure: hosts, services, DNS, proxies and the flows between them.
info.description:
Stackmap documents your infrastructure (hosts, services, DNS, proxies, VPNs) and the flows between
them. Every route is generated from its contract, so this reference is always the API itself.

## Errors

Errors follow [RFC 9457 Problem Details](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9457), as `application/problem+json`:
`type`, `title`, `status`, `detail` and `instance`, plus a stable `code` and, for invalid input, `issues`.
Translate errors with `code`, not with `title` or `detail`.

## Authentication

Operations need the session cookie (`better-auth.session_token`) that signing in sets, except public ones.

## Roles

Each operation states the role it needs (`x-required-role`): `public`, `signedIn` (any session),
`instanceAdmin`, or a role in the workspace of its path, `viewer` < `editor` < `admin` < `owner`. It is
checked before the input: `401` without a session, `403` below the role, and `404` for a workspace the caller is
not a member of, the same answer as for one that does not exist.

## Strings

Names and labels in responses are i18n keys, such as `extensions.core.name`: the interface translates them.

## Versioning

`info.version` is the version of the API, raised on breaking changes, not with every release of Stackmap.

get.summary: Check that the app and its database are up
get.description:
For the Docker healthcheck and uptime monitors: answers 200 when the app and its database answer, 503 otherwise. Why the database does not answer is in the server logs, never in the response.

Public: anyone can call it.

200.description: The app and its database are up

get.summary: Say whether the first administrator can be created
get.description:
`open` while no account exists and the setup window, counted from the server start, has not passed; `closed` once it has, until a restart; `done` once an account exists.

Public: anyone can call it.

post.description:
Creates the instance administrator, signs them in (the session cookie is set) and, when asked, adds the demo workspace. Only once, and only while setup is `open`; of two concurrent requests, one wins.

Public: anyone can call it.

code.description:
The kind of problem, stable and machine-readable so the interface can translate it:

- `validation_failed` (400): A path parameter, query parameter or body is invalid or missing; `issues` says which.
- `payload_too_large` (413): The body is over 1 MiB.
- `unsupported_media_type` (415): The body is not `application/json`.
- `unauthenticated` (401): The operation needs a session, and the request has none, or an expired or invalid one.
- `forbidden` (403): The session's role is below the one the operation requires.
- `invalid_origin` (403): A request that changes something was sent by a page of another origin than `BETTER_AUTH_URL`.
- `invalid_credentials` (401): No account has this email and password; which one is wrong is not said.
- `already_set_up` (409): An account exists: the first administrator can only be created once.
- `setup_closed` (403): The setup window, counted from the server start, has passed; restarting Stackmap opens it again.
- `too_many_requests` (429): Too many attempts from this address; `Retry-After` says how many seconds to wait.
- `workspace_not_found` (404): No workspace has this id, or the caller is not one of its members.
- `workspace_slug_taken` (409): Another workspace already uses this slug.
- `invitation_not_found` (404): No invitation has this link or id: it may have expired, been used or been revoked.
- `invitation_email_mismatch` (403): The invitation is for another email than the signed-in account's.
- `already_member` (409): The person with this email is already a member of the workspace.
- `member_not_found` (404): This user is not a member of the workspace.
- `last_owner` (409): The change would leave a workspace without an owner.
- `internal_error` (500): An unexpected error; the server logs have the details.
- `invalid_response` (500): Outside production only: the server answered something its contract does not declare.
